title: measure and settle the status budget after the dedup — tighten to 25ms or record honestly what was reached
action: Re-measure the status command on the pinned host-real fixture exactly as today — spawn-inclusive, at least 50 runs, cold and warm series both reported, the reference runtime's figure recorded alongside — and settle the budget honestly against decision e119fc8b, which set the interim 70 ms guard and named a follow-up targeting 20 ms after which the budget tightens to 25 ms. THE HEADROOM RULE, SETTLED HERE BECAUSE THE EARLIER DRAFT WAS UNSATISFIABLE (validation B5): the status gate at queen-bench/src/main.rs:397 is a strict `warm.p95_ms < budget_ms` (main.rs:287 is the ping gate, same strictness), so setting the budget TO the measured p95 makes the gate fail by construction. A budget is therefore always the measured warm p95 rounded UP to the next 5 ms multiple, plus one 5 ms step of headroom, and never below the target the measurement earns. Worked examples: a warm p95 of 18.4 ms yields 25 ms (the e119fc8b target is met and the budget is exactly the 25 ms it named); a warm p95 of 31.2 ms yields 40 ms; a warm p95 of 22.0 ms yields 30 ms. State the rule and the arithmetic in the report so the next reader can re-derive the number rather than trust it. TWO HONEST OUTCOMES, both acceptable, neither optional: (a) warm p95 reaches 20 ms or better — set the status budget to 25 ms per e119fc8b, keep the per-command split (ping keeps its own 5 ms floor; one shared budget is forbidden), update budget_source to name the superseding decision, and log the supersession with the measured evidence; or (b) warm p95 lands above 20 ms — apply the headroom rule to the measured number, log a decision recording that budget with the profile and the reason the 20 ms target was not reached, superseding e119fc8b's target rather than leaving an unmet promise standing in the record. Answering whether 20 ms is reachable at all IS this cell's deliverable; a real number either way is success. BUILD BEFORE MEASURING (validation W7): queen-bench does not depend on queen-bee as a cargo dependency and resolves the binary as a sibling of its own executable, so a bench run without a preceding workspace release build silently measures whatever stale binary is already on disk. The verify below builds first — never reorder it. The fixture is never shrunk and the measurement method never changes to make a number look better (D5). TIEBREAK BELOW 20 MS (cold-pickup minor): when the headroom rule and outcome (a) disagree — a warm p95 of 14 ms gives 15+5 = 20 ms by the rule while (a) names 25 ms — the RULE wins and the budget is the tighter number; e119fc8b's 25 ms is a ceiling for the met-target case, never a floor that discards earned headroom. PROFILE CAPTURE (cold-pickup minor): queen-bench emits the per-block profile only on a RED gate (main.rs:402 guards it behind !pass), so on a green run capture it yourself by running the status command with its profile flag against the same fixture root, and say in the report which way you obtained it.

truths: the workspace is release-built before the bench runs, so the measured binary is provably the current one and not a stale sibling
queen-bench --check runs at least 50 spawn-inclusive iterations on the size-pinned fixture and reports cold and warm percentiles plus the reference-runtime baseline, with the fixture floors unchanged

the status budget in code equals the headroom rule applied to the measured warm p95 — rounded up to the next 5 ms multiple plus one 5 ms step, never below the target the measurement earns — and the report shows the arithmetic
the per-command budget split survives: ping is still gated at its own 5 ms floor and status carries its own constant and its own budget_source
a decision is logged either way, superseding e119fc8b's interim number and citing the measured percentiles, so no unmet promise is left standing in the record
a per-block profile of one warm run is recorded showing where the remaining in-process time goes after the dedup
the CI perf-smoke number travels with the dev budget at D5's 3x runner-variance ratio (a 25 ms dev budget implies 75 ms CI), stated in the report and in the logged decision

prohibitions: Never shrink the fixture or change the measurement method to reach a number (D5)
Never collapse ping and status onto one shared budget
Never report only the warm series
Never set a budget below the headroom rule's result — a gate that fails on the run that set it is not a gate
No edits to .bee/bin/ or packages/bee/ (D1 freeze)

trace.outcome: Re-measured queen-bee status warm p95 after rust-port-23's read dedup: 4 independent spawn-inclusive passes (3x50 runs + 1x200 runs) landed 23.666-25.302 ms, canonical/confirmatory 24.467 ms (200-run) vs mean 24.543 ms across all passes -- ABOVE e119fc8b's 20ms follow-up target (outcome b). Applied the headroom rule to the measured number: ceil(24.467/5)*5 + 5 = 30ms. Logged decision 58ad0b5c superseding e119fc8b's unmet 25ms promise with the measured evidence and a per-block warm profile (build_recovery_block 53.5%, list_cells 24.3%, read_backlog_counts 10.0%, build_review_block/gix 3.8%). Updated STATUS_BUDGET_MS 70.0->30.0, budget_source string, and doc comments in crates/queen-bench/src/main.rs and bench.rs; CI perf-smoke figure now 90ms (D5 3x ratio preserved). ping's 5ms floor untouched, never collapsed with status. Verify green: warm p95 24.756ms < 30ms budget, pass:true.
